audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 are given to Ornn in both layers while their whys[] call Level 2 'your cleanest trade window of the lane' and say your pattern 'still out-grinds a two-point Ornn'. Level 6 is marked Skill while its why says his R 'hard-answers your engage' and gives him 'a longer CC chain than yours'.
audit.why: Ornn has no Brittle detonation until he has both Bellows Breath and Searing Charge ranked and a pillar to charge into, so Levels 2-3 are Maokai's only real trading window. At 6 Call of the Forge God is a two-hit knockup on a 140s cooldown that beats a single Nature's Grasp root, which is Ornn's row, not a coinflip.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 and 2 set to Maokai (6/10), row 4 set to Ornn (3/10), in both layers. That is also the packet chart.

audit.why: Four spikes present and each is real: Lvl 2-3 pre-Brittle window, Lvl 6 Call of the Forge God, 1st item off Living Forge's no-recall upgrades, Late as his scaling. The Living Forge point is the strongest one in the file — he reaches his item spike without giving up a wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the file names only Volcanic Rupture — Living Forge, Bellows Breath, Searing Charge and Call of the Forge God appear nowhere, and the Brittle combo is described only as 'his W' and 'his E pillar'. dontsFull[1] is titled 'Get brittle-procced' with a description that says nothing about Brittle. dosFull[0] also calls Volcanic Rupture a 'wall-knockup setup', which blurs which ability actually knocks up.
audit.why: Volcanic Rupture creates the magma pillar; Searing Charge (14/13.5/13/12.5/12s) is the charge that knocks up only when it collides with terrain — including that pillar. Bellows Breath applies Brittle on the final gout of flame. Two separate abilities and two separate dodges, and the file collapses them into one.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now describes the pillar as the terrain he charges into; dontsFull[1].d names Bellows Breath and Searing Charge in sequence; phases[2].why names the pillar; phases[4].why names Call of the Forge God; phases[5].why names Living Forge.

audit.why: Volcanic Rupture at 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s is correctly identified as the tracked cooldown, and the 9s rank-1 figure is now stated in dosFull[0].d.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Ornn contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Two weak Level 1 tanks with one ability each and no combo — the opener is decided by sapling and brush control.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Ornn's Volcanic Rupture is down.
edits.after: W root into Q knockback with a Sap Magic heal beats him before Brittle exists — your cleanest trade window of the lane.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Ornn must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Repeatable W-Q plus Sap Magic out-grinds a two-point Ornn who cannot yet detonate Brittle into his magma pillar.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Ornn's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God double-knockups and can clip your W dash mid-flight — his CC chain is longer, so never commit into a held R.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Volcanic Rupture's cooldown.
edits.after: Living Forge lets him upgrade items in lane with no recall — he spikes before your Bami line.

edits.before: Wall-knockup setup. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: The pillar he charges into for the knockup, 9s. Engage once it is down.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Bellows Breath applies Brittle; Searing Charge cashes it in a knockup.

notes: Four of Ornn's five ability names were absent from the entire matchup. The more useful fix is separating the combo: the file treated 'his Q' as the knockup when Volcanic Rupture only builds the pillar and Searing Charge is what knocks up on colliding with it — a player dodging the wrong half eats the whole thing. Chart rows 1, 2 and 4 flipped in matched pairs to agree with the file's own whys[].
